newsitem.title: GREECE: More fines in Greece's Delta scandal - commission.
newsitem.headline: More fines in Greece's Delta scandal - commission.

text.p: Greece's capital market commission said on Thursday it had fined construction company Atemke's managing director Thomas Georgakis 250 million drachmas ($943,000) for manipulative trading on shares of Parnassos in the Delta Securities scandal.

The commission also fined Atemke's vice-president Harilaos Georgakis 70 million drachmas, its public relations officer Petros Stathis 100 million and board members Antonia Georgaki and Helen Georgaki 30 million and 10 million drachmas respectively.
The decision was based on the findings of three international auditing firms which looked into the Delta Securities scandal which broke in November last year.
The commission said that Thomas and Harilaos Georgakis and Petros Stathis had a series of trades on shares of Parnassos which were pre-arranged.
"The trades aimed to manipulate the market in terms of price and spread false and inaccurate information on the supply and demand for the company's shares," a commission statement said.
"The trades of the individuals fined were also based on confidential information, a serious violation of existing regulations," it said.
In violation of insider trading rules there were also trades by all of the individuals fined in shares of construction company Atemke, a subsidiary of Parnassos, the commission said.

The fines totalling almost half a billion drachmas came after another 1.5 billion slapped on Delta Securities and three other individuals last Friday for manipulative trading in shares of textile firm Magrizos whose shares are still suspended from trade.
The commission noted that the fines were not related to any activities by the Parnassos and Atemke companies despite the fact that most of the individuals fined were senior management.
The close examination of the audit findings is continuing, it said.
